title: Group Words by Length
statement:
`std::map` keeps its keys sorted, and `operator[]` creates a missing entry
on first access -- together that makes it the natural tool for grouping.

## Your function

```
std::map<std::size_t, std::vector<std::string>>
GroupByLength(const std::vector<std::string>& words);
```

Return a map from each word length to the words of that length, **in the
order they appeared in `words`**. Duplicate words are kept, each time they
occur. An empty `words` gives an empty map.

## Watch out

- **`groups[word.size()]` creates the vector on first use** -- you do not
  need to check whether the key exists before calling `push_back` on it.
- **Keep input order inside each group.** Do not sort the words, and do not
  remove duplicates; `"to"` appearing twice appears twice.
- The map's own ordering (ascending length) is free -- never sort the
  outer structure yourself.

tests.name: an empty line gives no groups
mixed lengths, order inside a group is input order
tests.stdin: the quick brown fox jumps over a lazy dog

tests.name: duplicates are kept
tests.stdin: to be or not to be
tests.description: 'to' and 'be' each appear twice and must each appear twice.
